title: CDP GetUrlAsync uses Target.getTargetInfo to bypass busy renderer
desc: GetUrlAsync/GetTitleAsync now hit Target.getTargetInfo first (browser-side, ~ms) so heavy SPA pages cannot block Runtime.evaluate past the 10s timeout.
steps: Primary: SendAsync('Target.getTargetInfo', {targetId}, 3000) -- returns targetInfo.url and targetInfo.title from the browser process directly
Fallback: EvalAsync('window.location.href') / EvalAsync('document.title') -- legacy path with 3-retry/backoff in EvalAsync
Trigger case: ChatGptSendAndWait Phase 0 URL-drift check on jobkorea.co.kr loaded with Criteo + LogAnalytics + kakaoPixel scripts blocked the renderer JS thread for 10s+
Lesson: any read-only CDP operation that the browser knows directly (URL, title, target list, window bounds) should never go through Runtime.evaluate -- use the Browser/Target/Page domain commands

Affected commands: wkappbot ask gpt / wkappbot ask gemini / wkappbot ask claude -- any call site that uses GetUrlAsync or GetTitleAsync (ChatGptSendAndWait Phase 0 URL drift, AskCommands.Loop.SendWait, AskCommands.Gemini.Helpers, AskCommands.Claude).

Reproducing the original suggest: wkappbot ask gpt 'long question on a heavy SPA tab' -- before the fix, BUG-AUTO suggest fires with TimeoutException. After the fix, the URL drift check returns instantly. Use wkappbot speak 'verified' --bg to acknowledge resolution. The suggest workflow tracks this fix via wkappbot suggest show 2026-05-08T10:35:31.
author: claude
